+ +  M O R E   M A I L ! ! + +

  January, 1991     Page  Reply

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Roy Blundel, BIRMINGHAM



Dear Sir,

I have been trying to use the
TWO-COL program in Issue 29
without success. My setup is,
Spectrum+, +D interface and disc
drive and a Citizen 120 D
printer. Unfortunately it prints
my Tasword files diagonally
across the page,(please find
enclosed example). I have tried
altering the dip switches on my
printer to no avail. I have
enclosed photocopies of what I
hope are the relevant pages from
the manual. Please help, this is
driving me crazy...

I read in one of the earlier
Outlet issues you were trying to
write a program for printing out
graphs etc. in high res. I have
a program in my library files
which does just that, the
problem is that it came from a
now defunct Computer magazine
(ZX COMPUTING) and I am not sure
where I stand as regards to
copyright laws?


I also have a disc of short
programs from various sources
including a few of my own that I
am also not sure of... Many of
these programs where sent in by
readers of various magazines
under titles such as SHORT CUTS.

Now can you use these? it would
not be possible in most cases to
contact the original authors as
I no longer have their names.

Would you please give me your
advice as some of these programs
are quite good and it seems such
a shame that they may be lost to
us all.(except me of course)..

On another point, would it be
possible to print a list of
error report codes from JACKSOFT
as I keep geting confused as to
exactly what I have typed in
wrongly.

Could you explain in a little
more detail how you store code
in screen memory?

I have also had trouble in doing
a screen copy of certain
instruction pages to my printer
(The clip art program) as when I
press the button on the +D the
printer does not print the last
10 columns on each line, making
it d*!!*# hard to read them.

Last but not least, can you tell
me where I may be able to get a
double connector to conect Two
disc drives to my +D...

         Yours faithfully,

            Roy Blundel

To Roy Blundel from Brian Cavers

Try putting POKE 31526,8 at the
start of line 9878 in TWO-COL.
This should reduce the number of
spaces in the middle gap to 8.
Let me know how you get on.

We usually avoid programs from
old magazines that stopped pub-
lication even if copyright does
not seem to reside with anyone
any longer. It is a shame. They
probably couldn't care less -
the original authors may not
care or may even be pleased that
their software be used - the
trouble is in not being sure. I
have written to one or two
authors where the address is
given but with limited success.

JACKSOFT error codes are sparse
and, as far as I can tell,
undocumented. S-Error seems the
most common and refers to errors
like syntax, e.g., EX HL,DE
(should be EX DE,HL) but also if
a label is missing or a JR too
far to jump. I found P-Error is
if you define a message with no
end quotation mark, e.g....
DEFM "TEXT and I think I've seen
D-Error but could not pin it
down. Another common error is
not putting the space if no
label is needed so the opcode is
regarded as the label, e.g...
100 DJNZ  LOOP which may look ok
superficially.Sorry I can't help
more but that is a limitation of
JACKSOFT! Now Dr. Kode (OUTLET
39) gives better reports...

To store code in screen memory
you simply load it to an address
between 16384 and 23295. This is
only for a special use - e.g. if
the rest of memory may be in use
and you must remember that a CLS
or CLEAR -even a PRINT or scroll
will destroy the code! Have you
a special application in mind?


I do not know why your +D should
not do a full screen dump unless
it's because the right margin is
set? Just guessing. Try a full
reset of your system, load the
program direct and try again. It
is only a PRINT statement in the
program - there is nothing I can
think of to corrupt the +D.

I believe EEC LTD., 18-21
Misbourne House, Chiltern Hill,
Chalfont St. Peter,Bucks,SL9 9UE
(Tel 0753 888666)supply a double
connector lead to two drives for
about `15 but ring them first to
check.

                 - Brian Cavers

From J.L. Phillips, DORSET



Dear R & B,

In your preamble to the letters
section of OUTLET, you very
reasonably indicate that your
task of compiling your excellent
disk mag is considerably eased
by the submission of intended
contributions in textfile form.
Accordingly, I am sending you
this letter in SAM Tasword II
form on disc. I have two reasons
for this course of action. The
first is because it is what you
have requested. The second is
because it is relevant to the
main point of my letter.

Your correspondent, Mr Felstead,
[OUTLETTERS 39] was kind enough
to direct some praise at Issue 1
of the SAM SUPPLEMENT disc made
available through the SPECTRUM
DISCOVERY CLUB. However, he also
saw fit to comment adversely
upon the standards of spelling
and punctuation and this
observation calls for comment.

As a founder member of the
SPECTRUM DISCOVERY CLUB and one
of the three members primarily
involved in the production of
the SAM SUPPLEMENT, I was
particularly interested in the
criticism of the spelling and
punctuation because I spend some
considerable time on just those
aspects. There are two consider-
ations involved here...

First, if letters are received
in textfile form, much of the
advantage is lost if the letters
are to be edited before transfer
to the SUPPLEMENT. Moreover, a
letter is a personal contri-
bution and if the editor decides
to publish it, what right have I
to alter it in any way?

Secondly, as publication date
approaches, any delays for last
minute editing of late contri-
butions would result in delay in
issue of the disc, there is thus
a conflict between the desire
for perfection and expediency.
The standard eventually adopted
is a matter of judgement, not of
complacency.

Yes, Mr Felstead, the disc could
be perfect in all aspects of
punctuation and spelling.
However, so long as the disc is
technically accurate, produced
promptly by the voluntary
efforts of a few dedicated
enthusiasts and made available
to other enthusiasts at a cost
of no more than the postage, you
might be more understanding and
constructive in your criticism.
               J. L. Phillips

I know how you feel.After trying
hard, it's exasperating to hear
complaints.Still,Thurstan didn't
knock your EFFORTS or query your
MOTIVES. He reported what he saw
and was generally overwhelmingly
in favour - as I am!  - Brian C

To Steve Watson from Brian Gaff

Well,I think you are approaching
the problem from the wrong
angle. The drive sounds as if it
is sticking and, as the +D only
allows a certain time for the
head to reach the right place on
the disc, it simply gives the

spot of superglue fixed it.

Composite Video was easily extr-
acted from the old 48K machines
by taking the output from the
input to the modulator. The pin
needed being the one furthest
away from the edge of the PCB.
However, a +3 has a complication
which makes the signal unusable.

modulator, with a sound channel,
to the machine.Instead they used
a 6Mhz FM signal added to the
composite video, and shove both
into the input!I suggest you get
your expert to look up the data
sheets on the MC 1376 chip, as I
suspect there is a way of
extracting the composite signal
from it!            - Brian G.

From: Ian Ramage, GLASGOW

Dear Brian,

Your reply to D.A. Turton(OUTLET
39) would not help him to print
the ` sign using Tasprint, since
this uses the printer's graphics
capability to print different
fonts. He must configure his
Tasword program as follows:-

1. Use a backup copy of the
   program.

2. At the main menu, press C
   (Customise program).

3. At the sub menu, press T
   (Define print character
   translations).

4.If he now types the `
  character and presses<ENTER>,
  he will find that in the lower
  half of the screen, "#" is
  displayed, indicating that
  when the ` sign is pressed,the
  ASCII code for # is sent to
  the printer. This is O.K. when
  using Tasword on its own but
  not if Tasprint is being used.

5.Change the "#" to "`". (Don't
  delete the quotes.)

6.Press <ENTER> then <ENTER>
  again to return to sub menu.

7.Press <EDIT> to return to
  the main menu.

8.Press T to save the modified
  Tasword program.

That's all there is to it. Mr.
Turton does not state which
version of Tasword he is using.
Hopefully these instructions,
which are for the +3 version,
apply to the version which he is
using.

          Kind regards.

           I.A. Ramage






Many thanks, Ian
                  - Brian Cavers

ground on the difficult birth

Try putting POKE 31526,8 at the start of line 9878 in TWO-COL. This should reduce the number of spaces in the middle gap to 8. Let me know how you get on.

We usually avoid programs from old magazines that stopped pub- lication even if copyright does not seem to reside with anyone any longer. It is a shame. They probably couldn't care less - the original authors may not care or may even be pleased that their software be used - the trouble is in not being sure. I have written to one or two authors where the address is given but with limited success.

JACKSOFT error codes are sparse and, as far as I can tell, undocumented. S-Error seems the most common and refers to errors like syntax, e.g., EX HL,DE (should be EX DE,HL) but also if a label is missing or a JR too far to jump. I found P-Error is if you define a message with no end quotation mark, e.g.... DEFM "TEXT and I think I've seen D-Error but could not pin it down. Another common error is not putting the space if no label is needed so the opcode is regarded as the label, e.g... 100 DJNZ  LOOP which may look ok superficially.Sorry I can't help more but that is a limitation of JACKSOFT! Now Dr. Kode (OUTLET 39) gives better reports...

To store code in screen memory you simply load it to an address between 16384 and 23295. This is only for a special use - e.g. if the rest of memory may be in use and you must remember that a CLS or CLEAR -even a PRINT or scroll will destroy the code! Have you a special application in mind?

Composite Video was easily extr- acted from the old 48K machines by taking the output from the input to the modulator. The pin needed being the one furthest away from the edge of the PCB.
